cases.reason: Concrete paid apprenticeship with an application window open on the assignment date. Its four-year duration is training alongside employment; selection and the first paid assignment remain uncertain.
criticalDetails: Applications and supporting documents must be complete by September 30, 2026; the next opening is February 1, 2027. First email documents to djeatcapplications@outlook.com, allow up to one week for review, then follow the online application instructions. [Application instructions](https://djeatc68.com/apply/)

Required documents include a valid driver's license, second identification document, and evidence of high-school/GED/college graduation. The application costs $35, nonrefundable. The GAN personal-experience form must be completed within two weeks of its email invitation; selection depends on ranking after testing. [Application requirements](https://djeatc68.com/apply/)

Inside Wireman training lasts four years, normally combining a 40-hour contractor workweek with two evening classes weekly and occasional Saturdays. The page advertises starting pay of $22.70/hour, but its completion-pay figures conflict: $37.01/hour versus a stated current journeyman wage of $49.35. Confirm the applicable wage schedule. [Inside Wireman program](https://djeatc68.com/inside-wireman-apprenticeship/)

Applicants must travel to assigned jobsites throughout the jurisdiction. Inside Wireman applicants undergo background screening; a felony does not automatically disqualify them. Drug screening includes marijuana. The application fee requires a credit card. [Applicant FAQ](https://djeatc68.com/apply/applicant-faq/)
Local contact: 303-295-1903, 5610 Logan Street, Denver. [Provider contact](https://djeatc68.com/)
openQuestions: What are the current selection backlog and earliest possible paid contractor assignment?
What additional tuition, books, tools, dues, testing or repayment obligations apply?
What minimum age and other entry requirements apply, and what transportation arrangements are necessary?

cases.reason: Exclude as a stand-alone public employment referral. Published career counseling is part of residential addiction recovery; no separate nonresident job-help pathway was found. It remains potentially useful as an integrated recovery referral.
criticalDetails: Residents receive career counseling from their first day. Required employment must be permanent, full-time, tax-paying and compatible with program schedules; temporary, part-time and cash jobs are prohibited. The employer contact is for hiring residents, not evidence of public intake. [Work program](https://stepdenver.org/our-4-pillars/work/)

The residential program serves men aged 18 or older with addiction. Applicants must be sober at intake; Step does not provide detox. Its application page identifies restrictions involving certain severe violent or sexual offenses. [Admissions requirements](https://stepdenver.org/apply/)

Call 303-295-7837 or apply in person Monday–Friday, 7 a.m.–noon. Accepted applicants may enter at 2:30 p.m. that day, subject to bed availability. Entry is free; unspecified program fees begin after employment. [Program FAQ](https://stepdenver.org/program-faqs/)

Step reports that 79% obtain full-time employment within 45 days; this is a provider claim, not a guaranteed start date. Residency has no fixed duration, and a five-day orientation is strongly recommended. [Program FAQ](https://stepdenver.org/program-faqs/)
openQuestions: For an appropriate recovery referral, what are the actual post-employment fees and current bed availability?
Does Step offer any separate nonresident employment service? None was established in the reviewed sources.

cases.reason: Useful appointment-based coaching for Emily Griffith students and alumni, but the page does not establish general public access. Preserve the separate apprenticeship inquiry route.
criticalDetails: Career coaches assist students and alumni with resumes, interviews, job searches and applications. Online and in-person meetings require appointments. Email careerservices@emilygriffith.edu or use the scheduling link. [Career Services](https://www.emilygriffith.edu/career-services-for-job-seekers/)

Apprenticeship job seekers have a distinct appointment contact: apprenticeship@emilygriffith.edu. Prospective students are directed to admissions@emilygriffith.edu. [Intake routes](https://www.emilygriffith.edu/career-services-for-job-seekers/)

The college lists approved-employer postings alongside coaching, making this more than a generic job board for eligible users. Address: 1860 Lincoln Street, Denver. The page publishes neither a coaching fee nor appointment lead times or guaranteed placement. [Services and contact](https://www.emilygriffith.edu/career-services-for-job-seekers/)
openQuestions: Can unaffiliated community members receive coaching, and who qualifies for the apprenticeship appointment route?
Are appointments free, and how soon can an eligible person meet a coach?

cases.reason: Current government evidence confirms Denver Day Works continues under ServiceSource, but the supplied Bayaud listing needs updating and a current program-specific intake route was not verified.
criticalDetails: Denver adopted a ServiceSource contract amendment on May 18, 2026, extending Denver Day Works funding through December 31, 2026 for participant wages, support and operations. This establishes current program funding, not an available work slot. [Adopted city resolution](https://denver.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?G=928A1C29-26D7-4A5D-8DD4-947A533B1CC6&GUID=C2549384-7B0D-4074-8F30-B120C114EBEE&ID=7974114&Options=&Search=)

ServiceSource announced that it was integrating programs and staff formerly operated by Bayaud. The supplied Bayaud homepage returned no useful service information. [Successor announcement](https://servicesource.org/servicesource-launches-new-programs-in-colorado/)

Historical Bayaud materials describe case-manager intake before work, followed by employment assistance, cash payouts and bus passes beginning in week one, with training and clothing support during later weeks. This supports an early-help model rather than waiting until program completion, but does not verify today's schedule. [Historical program schedule](https://bayaudenterprises.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Denver-Day-Works-Website-8-2-24.pdf)

A 2024 flyer lists Monday 1 p.m. orientations at Colorado Village Collaborative, 1530 W. 13th Avenue, except Monday holidays. Treat this as unconfirmed historical intake information. [Historical orientation flyer](https://bayaudenterprises.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/Denver-Day-Works-Website-4-23-24.pdf)

ServiceSource's general inquiry route is communications@servicesource.org or 800-244-0817; this can be used to request the current Denver Day Works contact. The newer city presentation could not be retrieved within the source-page budget. [Successor contact](https://www.servicesource.org/contact-us/)
openQuestions: What are the current orientation address, schedule, direct contact and enrollment process?
What homelessness, residency, disability, work-authorization or documentation requirements apply?
What are the current wage, payout schedule, participant costs, available shifts and delay before first paid work?

cases.reason: Actionable local reentry pathway combining employment assistance with paid transitional work. A referral requirement is manageable through the named intake process.
criticalDetails: CEO Denver serves people recently released from incarceration. Contact CEODenver@ceoworks.org or 720-279-8489; office: 3532 Franklin Street, Suite S, Denver, Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m. [Denver office](https://www.ceoworks.org/locations/denver)

CEO says it can help people under community supervision obtain a parole/probation officer referral. After referral, CEO invites the person to the next scheduled orientation. Outside California, orientation requires a completed referral form, release form, government photo ID, and Social Security card or birth certificate. [Participant intake](https://www.ceoworks.org/participants)

The national program model includes immediate paid transitional work, job-readiness training, coaching and placement. This describes help after enrollment, not a guaranteed Denver start date upon inquiry. [Program model](https://www.ceoworks.org/)

CEO provides employer outreach and retention support for one year after full-time employment. The public intake page does not specify Denver wages, fees, orientation dates or current capacity. [Participant services](https://www.ceoworks.org/participants)
openQuestions: How recent must release be, and can someone not currently on supervision enroll?
When are the next orientation and first paid shift, and is orientation itself paid in Denver?
What wages, participant costs, transportation assistance and help obtaining missing documents currently apply?

cases.reason: Preserve as a targeted CDOC referral for paid transitional work and employment support, with current operating details requiring confirmation.
criticalDetails: Eligibility requires existing participation in CDOC employment-readiness transition programming; recruitment and selection run through CDOC and the named operator, Bayaud. Practical first step: ask the person's CDOC transition contact about New Heights. DEN also provides a CEEA inquiry form. [Program and inquiry form](https://www.flydenver.com/business-and-community/ceea/career-pathways/new-heights-pilot-program/)

DEN describes 12-week paid work placements and career-finding assistance while waitlisted. Twelve weeks is the placement duration, not a stated pre-work delay. The page lists $23.75/hour but inconsistently describes weekly compensation and daily payment, and a waitlist threshold above 10 versus capacity of 20. [Program FAQ](https://www.flydenver.com/business-and-community/ceea/career-pathways/new-heights-pilot-program/)

Published supports include meals, boots, uniforms, tools, van transport and an RTD EcoPass where needed. Work is outside secure airport areas; background review still applies. No participant fee is stated. [Work and supports](https://www.flydenver.com/business-and-community/ceea/career-pathways/new-heights-pilot-program/)
openQuestions: Who currently operates intake following ServiceSource's takeover of former Bayaud programs, and are referrals being accepted?
What are the actual capacity, wait time, wage and payment frequency?
What exact CDOC criteria, work schedule and transportation pickup arrangements apply?

cases.reason: Useful free career-advancement navigation for eligible immigrants and refugees with financial stability. It explicitly does not provide immediate job placement.
criticalDetails: First step: email immigrant.services@emilygriffith.edu with name, phone and career background or goal for eligibility screening and orientation. Navigation typically runs 1–2 years, with weekly or biweekly meetings during business hours, online or in person. First-appointment delay is unspecified. [CAREERS](https://www.emilygriffith.edu/careers-for-refugees-and-immigrants/)

The page lists eligibility routes involving current Emily Griffith English levels 4/5, interest in its CTE programs, or foreign engineering/barbering/cosmetology experience. It also requires intermediate English, work authorization or a pathway to employment, and a job or other financial stability. [Eligibility](https://www.emilygriffith.edu/careers-for-refugees-and-immigrants/)

Services include career planning, licensing/education navigation, credential-evaluation guidance, coaching and scholarships. Participation is free for eligible students; training and evaluation expenses are not universally stated to be covered. [Services and costs](https://www.emilygriffith.edu/careers-for-refugees-and-immigrants/)
openQuestions: How are the eligibility bullets applied, particularly for people planning training outside Emily Griffith?
When is the next orientation, and which training, licensing and credential-evaluation costs would remain payable?

cases.reason: Important disability-employment referral with continuing eligibility assessment and referral help. New applicants should expect a service waitlist rather than immediate funded job coaching or placement.
criticalDetails: DVR supports people with disabilities seeking to obtain, retain or advance in employment. Potential services include counseling, training, job development/coaching, benefits planning and assistive technology, tailored to individual needs. [DVR services](https://dvr.colorado.gov/)

The January 28, 2026 announcement places newly eligible people and eligible participants without an established employment plan on a waitlist. Eligibility assessment continues; waitlisted people receive information about other resources. Existing employment plans and students already receiving pre-employment transition services continue. [Waitlist announcement](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/CODLE/bulletins/4065f78)

The April 8, 2026 newsletter confirms an active waitlist exceeding 2,100 people at that time. No later release timeline was verified; this number is historical, not a September count. [April update](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/CODLE/bulletins/40dedf6)

Contact Denver intake at 303-866-2500 or cdle_denverdvrfrontdesk@state.co.us; the office directory lists 2211 W. Evans, Denver. The website also links an online service request, but that form could not be verified during this research. [Office directory](https://dvr.colorado.gov/contact-us/)

Current participant cost-sharing was not established. The linked 2026 handbook exposed only its viewer, so do not promise that every training expense or purchased support is free. [DVR-linked handbook](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1q9kDb3gdgBshWVdXZgPPRUlInXkDRKjE/view?usp=sharing)
openQuestions: What is the current waitlist status for the person's priority category, and when might services begin?
What documentation and assessment appointments are required, and which referral services are available while waiting?
Which requested services require financial contribution or other funding, and what accessibility or transportation assistance is available?
